title: Momentum and Newton's second law
main_stem: A block is pulled in a straight line along a rough horizontal surface by a varying force $X$, as shown in Fig. 3.1. [Fig. 3.1 shows block with momentum $p$ and force $X$ to the right on rough horizontal surface]. Air resistance is negligible. Assume that the frictional force exerted on the block by the surface is constant and has magnitude $2.0\,\mathrm{N}$. The variation with time $t$ of the momentum $p$ of the block is shown in Fig. 3.2. [Fig. 3.2: $p / \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ vs $t / \mathrm{s}$, straight line from $(0,0)$ to $(4.0,6.0)$, then horizontal at $6.0$ to $6.0\,\mathrm{s}$].

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Newton's second law of motion.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: Use Fig. 3.2 to determine, for the block at time $t = 2.0\,\mathrm{s}$, the magnitude of:
parts.text: the resultant force on the block

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: On Fig. 3.3, sketch a graph to show the variation of force $X$ with time $t$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 6.0\,\mathrm{s}$. [Fig. 3.3: $X / \mathrm{N}$ vs $t / \mathrm{s}$, $X$ 0 to 4.0, $t$ 0 to 6].

marking_points.text: (resultant force on object) is proportional to / equal to the rate of change of momentum
horizontal line at any non-zero value of $X$
